title: Retention of the Loss-of-Use Charge on an Excess Flood Sale Cancellation
content:
When an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** policy is cancelled for the sale of the home, part of the tier's loss-of-use charge may be kept back from the returned premium.

## Rule

The loss-of-use charge retention keeps back the tier's loss-of-use charge times the unexpired days over the days of the term, in full where the latest loss-of-use payment on the policy's claims was issued on or after the term start, at half where the latest one was issued before the term start, and not at all where no loss-of-use payment was ever issued.

Each retention or charge set on a sale cancellation is subtracted from the returned premium — once that premium has been limited to the term premium less the minimum earned share, and before its single rounding to the cent — and the returned premium never falls below nothing.

The unexpired days are those counted for the returned premium. The latest loss-of-use payment is the loss-of-use payment issued most recently on any claim of this excess policy. Where two entries on a file share the date they are read by, or two policy records answer the same description, the one entered first is read.

| Latest loss-of-use payment on the policy's claims | Retention |
|---|---|
| issued on or after the term start | the whole charge times the unexpired days over the days of the term |
| issued before the term start | half (0.5) of that amount |
| none ever issued | nothing |

## Worked illustration (hypothetical figures, not a tier's)

A loss-of-use charge of 120.00 and 265 unexpired days in a 365-day term: the full retention is 120.00 times 265 over 365, about 87.12 (it is not rounded on its own); at half it is about 43.56. Taken from an unrounded returned premium of about 1452.05, the full retention leaves 1364.93 after the single rounding to the cent.
